ORDER:

1. Complainant Gulsheen Kaur has filed the present revision petition challenging the impugned order dated 26.06.2023 whereby Ld. MM(Mahila Court)-02 West had discharged all the accused persons for offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC and accused Iqbal Singh for offence u/s 377 IPC in case FIR No. 512/2021, PS Tilak Nagar.
2. The Respondents no. 2 to 5 in the present revision petition are the accused persons who were chargesheeted before Ld. Trial Court in case FIR No. 512-2021, PS Tilak Nagar.
State has been impleaded as Respondent no.1 in the present revision petition.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court.
3. Arguments on the revision petition have been heard.
Record carefully perused.

BRIEF FACTS 4. Brief facts of the case necessary for disposing off the present revision petition are that the present FIR was registered on 30.06.2021 on the basis of a type written complaint dated 11.03.2021 running into 15 pages made by complainant Gulsheen Kaur against her husband Iqbal Singh (A-1), her father in law Darshan Singh (A-2), her mother in law Jasbir Kaur (since deceased and not chargesheeted),
her sister in law Ravinder Kaur (A-3) and her brother in law Harpreet Singh(A-4) alleging commission of offences u/s 323/341/351/354/377/498A/406/506/509/34 IPC.
5.
During investigation, statement of the complainant was also recorded u/s 164 CrPC.
After completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against accused Iqbal Singh and Darshan Singh for offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
In addition, accused Iqbal Singh was also chargesheeted for offence u/s 377 IPC.
Accused Ravinder Kaur was chargesheeted for offence u/s 406/34 IPC while accused Harpreet Singh was chargesheeted for offence u/s 406/34 and 354 IPC.
Chargesheet was filed without arrest of the accused persons on 25.10.2021.
6. After appearance of the accused persons, they were admitted to regular court bail.
Ld. Trial Court heard the arguments on the point of charge from the accused persons, Ld. APP for the State as well as Ld. Counsel for the complainant.

IMPUGNED ORDER:
7.

After hearing the arguments on the point of charge, Ld. Trial Court discharged all the accused persons for offence u/s 498A/34 IPC holding that the entire complaint was filled with general allegations.
There was not even a single allegation against the accused persons of having demanded any dowry or any subsequent harrassment given by them to the complainant for the non-fulfilment of said demands.

Ld. Trial Court noted that the complaint was filed after almost 14 years of marriage and during these 14 years, there was no specific complaint made by the complainant against her in laws regarding the cruelties inflicted upon her by them on account of non-fulfilment of dowry demands.

sentences.text: Considering specific allegations regarding an incident dated 13.11.2016, charge u/s 354 r/w 354A IPC was directed to be framed against accused Harpreet Singh (A-4).

9. As regards offence u/s 406 IPC, Ld. Trial Court observed that the allegations were made in the complaint that A-3 had forced her to leave her entire jewellery with her on the pretext of keeping the same in safe custody.
However, the complainant had nowhere alleged in her complaint that A-3/Ravinder Kaur had refused to return her streedhan articles on her demand.
Accordingly, Ld.
Trial Court observed that no prima facie case u/s 406 IPC was made out as the ingredients of the offence were not complete.

Accordingly, accused persons were discharged for offence u/s 406/34 IPC.
10.
As regards offence u/s 377 IPC, Ld. Trial Court observed that there was no specific allegation against Iqbal Singh(A-1) that he had subjected the complainant to unnatural sex at any point of time.
The complainant was also medically examined on 12.07.2021 but no injury was found on her person.
Thus, accused Iqbal Singh was also discharged for offence u/s 377 IPC.
GROUNDS OF REVISION / ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF COMPLAINANT 11.
In the present revision petition, complainant has challenged the impugned order dated 26.02.2023 on the ground that the same is legally erroneous and contrary to facts of the case and settled law.
Ld. Trial Court has passed the impugned order in a haste without giving an opportunity to the complainant to depose before the Court and by taking a hypertechnical approach.
It is submitted that grave error of law has been committed in appreciating the facts of the case.
Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that at the stage of framing of charge, there is no need to doubt the sufficiency of evidence to convict the accused.
Materials brought on record by the prosecution can be believed to be true at the stage of charge and their probative value cannot be decided at this stage.
The impugned order is based on conjectures and surmises.
Despite specific allegations made in the complaint, the accused persons have been discharged.
Ld. Trial Court has also failed to appreciate statement of the complainant recorded u/s 164 CrPC wherein also, specific allegations have been made against the accused persons.
Counsel for the complainant/revisionist has argued in line with the grounds of revision.
He has relied upon the following citations in support of his arguments.

(a) State Vs J.Doraiswamy AIR 2019 SC 1518 to stress upon the point that at the stage of consideration of discharge of accused, the court has to proceed with the assumption that the material brought on record by the prosecution is true and Court has to find out if the material on record taken on its face value discloses the ingredients of the alleged offence and the court is not required to go deep into the matter as would be required for conviction.
(b) State of Maharashtra Vs Salman Khan 2004 Crl LJ 920 (SC) wherein the Apex Court has observed that the assessment of truthfulness, sufficiency and acceptability of material produced on record cannot be done at the time of framing of charges.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF ACCUSED PERSONS//RESPONDENTS NO. 2 TO 5:
14.
Per contra, the accused persons/Respondents no. 2 to 5 have supported the impugned order stating that it is a well reasoned order based on material available on record.
There is no infirmity and illegality in the impugned order.

All the allegations made in the complaint have been carefully perused by Ld. Trial Court while passing the impugned order and it has been rightly held that there are no specific allegations against any of the accused persons.
A detailed written reply has been filed on behalf of the respondents.

It is submitted that the impugned order is not a mechanical order passed in a routine manner and clearly shows application of mind as all the accused persons have not been discharged rather charges have been directed to be framed against accused Harpreet Singh for offences u/s 354/354A IPC.
It is submitted that even in the present revision petition, no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order has been pointed out, rather again general allegations have been made.

Ld. Trial Court has rightly observed that the complaint on the basis of which, FIR has been registered has been drafted in a manner and with a mindset to implicate the accused persons under as many criminal offences as possible.
However, there are no specific allegations and the essential ingredients of the alleged offences are lacking in the allegations made in the complaint.
It is submitted that there is no merit in the present revision petition and the same should be dismissed with a heavy cost.

15. Ld. Counsel for the respondents have relied upon the following decisions of the superior courts in support of her arguments:
(a) Ajay Gupta Vs State of Haryana, Crl Appeal No. 2379/2024, order dated 03.05.2024 passed by the Apex Court on 03.05.2024 wherein an FIR registered in matrimonial cases with general allegations was quashed by the Apex Court.
(b) Ashwani Kumar Vs State of UP, Application u/s 482 CrPC no. 1759/2022, order dated 07.02.2022 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad.

383.

sentences.text: Relying upon these citations, it is submitted that it is the duty of the court to avoid misuse of criminal justice system especially in matrimonial cases where the attempt is to implicate as many relatives of the husband as possible in as many offences as possible.
It is submitted that the present complaint is a classic example of such misuse of matrimonial laws.
By making general allegations in a bulky complaint running into 50 paragraphs, the complainant has tried to falsely implicate all the relatives of the husbands in several offences.
However, Ld. Trial Court has rightly appreciated the complaint and the allegations made therein and discharged the accused persons vide impugned order dated 26.06.2023
as essential ingredients of the alleged offences were not reflected from the complaint.
In these circumstances, there is no reason for interfering in the impugned order.

Hence,
dismissal of the present revision petition is prayed.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/RESPONDENT NO.1:
17.
On behalf of the State, Ld. Additional PP has also supported the impugned order dated 26.06.2023.
It is submitted that it is a well reasoned order passed on the basis of allegations made in the complaint and material collected during investigation.
There is no infirmity or illegality in the same and there is no reason for interfering with the impugned order dated 26.06.2023.

Hence,
dismissal of the present revision petition is sought.
FINDINGS:
18. I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record.

19. The scope of enquiry, a judge is required to make while considering the question of framing of charges has been considered by the Apex Court in Union of India Vs.
Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4 .

entities.text:
Union of India Vs.
Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After an exhaustive survey of the case law on the point, the Apex court has laid down the following principles:-
" (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be, fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would be naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however, if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

Gulsheen Kaur vs State Of Nct Delhi on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40307612/
5 (4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouth-piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.

sentences.text:
This however,
does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."
20. Section 498A IPC provides punishment for cruelty to a woman by her husband or relative of her husband.
The term cruelty within the meaning of Section 498A IPC has been explained in the explanation to the said section.
It consists of two clauses (a) and (b).

To attract Section 498A IPC, it must be established that the cruelty or harassment to wife was to force her to cause grave bodily injury to herself or to commit suicide; or the harassment was to compel her to fulfill illegal demands of dowry.

Thus, every type of harassment or cruelty would not attract Section 498A IPC.
21.
22. Section 406 IPC provides punishment for the offence of criminal breach of trust defined under Sec. 405 IPC.

There are two essential ingredients for the offence of criminal breach of trust first being entrustment with property or dominion over property and the second is dishonest misappropriation of the property.
Both these ingredients are required to be present before an offence of criminal breach of trust punishable under Sec. 406 IPC can be held to be prima facie made out.

23. I have carefully perused the complaint on the basis of which present FIR has been registered as well as the documents annexed with the chargesheet and the statement of witnesses recorded u/s 161 CrPC and that of complainant recorded u/s 164 CrPC.

24. Considering the overall material available on record, no infirmity or illegality is found in the impugned order dated 26.06.2023 discharging the accused persons from the offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC as well as discharging accused Iqbal Singh for offence u/s 377 IPC.

I find no infirmity or illegality in the reasoning given by Ld. Trial Court while discharging the accused persons as clearly no specific incident of dowry demand or harassment given to the complainant at Gulsheen Kaur vs State Of Nct Delhi on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40307612/
6 the hands of any of the accused persons for fulfillment of the said dowry demands has been stated by the complainant in her complaint or by any of the relatives of the complainant in their statements recorded u/s 161 CrPC.

sentences.text: Neither any specific incident has been narrated nor there is any MLC of the complainant on record in respect of harassments given to her.
Although, there are allegations made in the complaint regarding the tauntings given by the accused persons for bringing insufficient and low quality dowry articles/gifts in marriage.
However, there is no allegation that any demand for any specific dowry article was made from her or she was harrassed for non-fulfilment of the said dowry demand.

General allegations like abuse of the complainant by using choicest words followed by physical abuse have been made without making any specific allegation as to the reason for which the said abuse was done.

The only specific allegations that are contained in the entire complaint are allegations against accused Harpreet Singh(A-4) for offences u/s 354/354A IPC for which he has been directed to be charged.

Even in the statement of the complainant recorded u/s 164 CrPC, the complainant had not made any allegation of any dowry demands made by the accused persons from her or any kind of harrassment given to her on account of non-fulfilment of the said dowry demands.
Statements of the parents of the complainant i.e. her father Harbhajan Singh and her mother Ravinder Kaur have also been recorded u/s 161 CrPC.
Perusal of the same also shows that although, there are allegations of taunting made in their statements, but there are no specific allegations of any dowry demands made by the accused persons.
Thus, the essential ingredients for making a prima facie case u/s 498A IPC are not reflected from the material available on record.

Mere allegations of taunts for bringing insufficient dowry or low quality gifts in marriage without corresponding allegations of harassment to the complainant for fulfillment of any dowry demand are not sufficient for attracting offence under Sec. 498A IPC.
This is more so in the present case as even the allegations of taunting are vague and without any date, month or year.

25. As regards offence under Sec. 406 IPC, clearly there is not even a single averment or evidence on record to show that any article belonging to the deceased was ever entrusted to any of the accused persons or has been misappropriated by them.
The only allegation made in the entire complaint is that while moving to Pune, the complainant had handed over her jewellery articles to accused Ravinder Kaur for safe custody on her asking.
However, there is no allegation that accused Ravinder Kaur or any other accused persons had misappropriated the said jewellery articles or refused to return the same to the complainant on demand.
Thus, no prima facie case under Sec. 406 IPC is attracted against any of the accused persons.

26. As regards offence u/s 377 IPC, again, no infirmity or illegality is observed in the impugned order dated 26.06.2023 and the accused Iqbal Singh has been rightly discharged for offence u/s 377 IPC as the allegations are general in nature without support of any medical documents.
27.

It was also submitted on behalf of the complainant during the course of arguments that her counsel has not been heard on the point of charge and some random counsel, Sh. Akshay Kumar Saini has been marked as present for the complainant in ordersheet dated 26.06.2023.
it has been submitted that this also shows that the impugned order has been passed without due application of mind or without hearing the counsel for the complainant.
I have carefully perused the record in this regard.

Although, it is correct that attendance of Sh. Akshay Kumar Saini, Advocate has been marked as appearing for complainant in ordersheet dated 26.06.2023 but the arguments on the Gulsheen Kaur vs State Of Nct Delhi on 3 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40307612/
7 point of charge were not heard on that day.

entities.text: Gulsheen Kaur vs State Of Nct Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rather, the arguments on the point of charge were heard on 19.10.2022 wherein attendance of Sh. Anil Kumar Gupta, Ld. Counsel for the complainant has been duly marked.
Even in subsequent ordersheets, attendance of Sh. Anil Kumar Gupta, Advocate has been marked for the complainant.

Accordingly, attendance of Sh. Akshay Kumar Saini, Advocate in ordersheet dated 26.06.2023 might be a typographical error, however, it does not affect the validity of the impugned order as the arguments on the point of charge were not heard on 26.06.2023 on which date matter was reserved for orders only.
28. Perusal of the impugned order clearly shows that it is not a mechanical order passed in a routine manner.

Impugned order clearly shows due application of mind as neither charge has been directed to be framed against all the accused persons, nor all the accused persons have been discharged,
rather charges have been appropriately framed and certain accused persons have been rightly discharged by a well reasoned order.
The entire material on record taken on its face value fails to disclose the essential ingredients of offences u/s 498A/406 IPC.
Thus, the accused persons have been rightly discharged.

29. Considering the overall material available on record and the reasons given by Ld. Trial Court in the impugned order dated 26.06.2023, I am of the opinion that the accused persons have been rightly discharged by Ld. Trial Court.
No infirmity or illegality is observed in the impugned order dated 26.06.2023.
30. In view of the reasons given above, I find no merit in the present revision petition.
The same is accordingly, dismissed and the impugned order dated 26.06.2023 is upheld.
31. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order.
